title: Julius Caesar Kidnapped by Pirates (75 BC)
overlooked_twist: Pirates demanded 20 talents ($20M). Caesar laughed, said he was worth 50 talents, ordered them to be quiet so he could sleep, made them listen to his speeches, and warned them with a grin he would crucify them. 38 days later, ransom paid, he raised a private fleet, hunted them down, and kept his exact promise.
wikipedia_summary: In 75 BC, Julius Caesar was captured by Cilician pirates in the Aegean Sea while traveling to Rhodes. Plutarch reports that when the pirates asked for a ransom of twenty talents of silver, Caesar insisted they demand fifty. After the ransom was paid and he was freed, Caesar raised a fleet at Miletus, captured the pirates, and executed them as he had promised during captivity.

scholarly_papers.title: Pirates in the Ancient World
scholarly_papers.summary: Analysis of Mediterranean maritime piracy and the ransom protocols under Roman civil law.
